what_it_does: Spin qubits (a type of quantum bit based on electron spin) need to be read out quickly and accurately, and scaling from dozens to thousands requires reading many qubits simultaneously without massive power budgets. This chip reads multiple spin qubits using quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM)—a radio technique that encodes two independent signals on the same frequency by using two perpendicular phase alignments—so many qubits can report their state on one carrier wave. The design achieves just 18.5 microwatts per qubit in a cryogenic environment (near absolute zero) by using a capacitive feedback amplifier instead of bulky inductors.
